evals.name: headless-dispatch-contract
evals.prompt: I'm about to be dispatched as a headless CI agent against an issue in one of the fleet repos. Before I touch anything, walk me through the behavioral contract I'm expected to follow: how I identify myself, how I claim or take over the issue, what progress and parking look like, and what the hard limits are. Just describe the rules, don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: Grounds the answer in the canonical reference/agent-protocol.md: the console already posts the eyes reaction and claims the issue, progress goes through lcars session title/status rather than issue comments, parking ends with PARK and one marker-stamped comment, and the situational index is read only when its situation arises.
assertions: Grounds the rules in the skill's reference/agent-protocol.md, naming it as the source of the full protocol
Says the situational sections (such as CI reruns or the bot-identity assignment gotcha) are read only when that situation arises, not up front
Says the takeover claim and eyes reaction are already done by the console, so the agent posts nothing for them
Says progress is reported through `lcars session title` / `lcars session status`, not through issue comments
Describes parking as ending the response with `PARK <blocker and resume trigger>` and leaving one marker-stamped comment (or equivalent durable evidence) rather than going silent

evals.name: edit-dispatch-prompt-consumer-repo
evals.prompt: I want to tweak the prompt we hand to bot runs in the sprinkles repo so they stop posting a status comment every five minutes. Where is the behavior that governs how those bot runs behave actually defined, and what should I check before changing the prompt text in the consuming repo?
evals.expected_output: Explains that fleet behavior is defined once in Agent LCARS's shared agent-protocol (reference/agent-protocol.md), which consumers resolve rather than copy; that the protocol already forbids progress comments (progress goes to lcars session status), so periodic comments mean an override or an older copy; and that a fleet-wide rule change belongs in the canonical protocol while a sprinkles-only rule belongs in sprinkles' own AGENTS.md or prompt.
assertions: Identifies the shared agent-protocol skill owned by Agent LCARS (its reference/agent-protocol.md) as the single canonical definition, not a copy kept in sprinkles
States that consuming repositories do not download, copy or hardcode the protocol; the runner resolves it from its own bundled skill tree

Notes that the protocol already routes progress through `lcars session status` (or otherwise says agents should not post progress comments), so periodic status comments point to a local override, an outdated copy or a non-agent workflow
Recommends changing a fleet-wide rule in the canonical protocol and a sprinkles-only rule in sprinkles' own instructions, rather than patching a per-repo copy

evals.name: lost-baseline-judgement-call
evals.prompt: I'm a dispatched fleet worker on issue #812 in implement mode. The acceptance criteria say to compare the new job's runtime against last month's baseline run, but that run's logs were deleted by retention. I have a fresh measurement of the new job only. Should I park and ask Joe to approve skipping the comparison? If not, what should my deliverable look like? Describe the plan; don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: Does not park: a lost baseline is a judgement call the worker makes. It states the decision and its evidence in the deliverable, delivers as partial work with `Tracks #812` rather than `Fixes #812` unless it judges acceptance met, and stamps the attempt-claim marker on the deliverable.
assertions: Decides not to park: treats the lost baseline as a judgement call the worker makes itself, not a blocker that needs maintainer approval
Says the deliverable must state the decision and the evidence it rests on
Says imperfect evidence is delivered as partial work referencing `Tracks #812` instead of `Fixes #812`, unless the worker judges acceptance actually met
Says the deliverable (for example the PR description) carries the run's attempt-claim marker

evals.name: ready-implementation-awaiting-review
evals.prompt: My dispatched implementation produced its own attempt-marked draft PR on a protected target. The closing scope and required independent local source review passed. There are no unresolved findings or deliberate holds. CI is running, GitHub requires another account to approve, and the brief has no handoff capability flag. What do I do on a GitHub issue dispatch? Would native Work differ?
evals.expected_output: For either implementation anchor, verify closing references, mark ready and arm protected squash auto-merge. Read back the arm and hand off the exact PR through the authenticated finalizer while CI and independent GitHub approval are pending.
assertions: Does not park, keep a draft, or wait for a brief capability flag or pending GitHub approval before readying either eligible implementation PR
Preserves local independent source review, deliberate holds, closing-reference verification and feedback guards
Hands off the exact marked PR with verified squash arming and lets branch protection enforce approval and CI before merge
